title: Discover vertebrates and invertebrates!
summary: Practise telling animals with backbones from animals without them.
keyIdeas: Vertebrates have an internal skeleton with a backbone.
Invertebrates have no backbone. Some have a shell or a hard outer covering.
Humans are vertebrates because we have backbones.

basicKnowledge: A. Cultura científica › Iniciación en la actividad científica
A. Cultura científica › La vida en nuestro planeta

activities.explanation: Vertebrates have an internal skeleton with a backbone. It can be made of bone or cartilage.

activities.prompt: Choose the word that completes the sentence.
activities.explanation: Invertebrates have no backbone. A hard outer covering does not make an animal a vertebrate.
A dog has bones and a backbone. Earthworms and jellyfish are invertebrates.
activities.hint: Think about which animal has a skeleton inside.

activities.prompt: Sort each animal into the right group.
activities.explanation: Cats, birds and fish are vertebrates. Snails, ants and butterflies have no backbone.

activities.prompt: Read carefully and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: A sparrow has an internal skeleton with bones. A ladybird is an insect with no backbone.
activities.title: Lucía and Hugo's walk
activities.text: Lucía and Hugo walk through the park. Lucía watches a sparrow on a branch. Hugo finds a ladybird on a leaf. They write in their notebook about each animal's body.

questions.explanation: A sparrow is a bird, and birds are vertebrates.

questions.prompt: Why is the ladybird an invertebrate?
questions.explanation: Ladybirds are insects with no bones or backbone.

activities.prompt: Aisha makes a mistake. Which statement is wrong?
activities.explanation: A snail's shell protects it on the outside. It is not an internal skeleton with bones.
activities.hint: Having a shell does not mean having bones inside.
options: Snails are vertebrates because they have a hard shell
Bony fish have bones in their skeleton

activities.explanation: Our backbone is part of our internal skeleton. This makes us vertebrates.

activities.prompt: A fossil has a backbone and other bones. Which animal could it have been?
activities.explanation: A fish can have a backbone and other bones. Octopuses and jellyfish have no backbone.
activities.hint: Think about which animal can have a bony skeleton.

activities.prompt: Put Martina's steps for studying a playground animal in order.
activities.explanation: Looking soft or hard is not enough to classify an animal. We observe it and check a guide to find out whether it has a backbone.
items: Watch the animal without touching or disturbing it
With an adult, check a guide to find out whether it has a backbone
Write down whether it is a vertebrate or an invertebrate
